desc:
Format a paragraph into lines of exactly width characters. The paragraph is the string words: lowercase words separated by single commas, in reading order.

Pack words greedily: put as many consecutive words as possible on a line, with at least one space between neighbouring words, without exceeding width. Then pad every line to exactly width characters:

  • A line with two or more words that is not the last line is justified: the extra spaces are spread as evenly as possible over the gaps between words. If they do not divide evenly, the gaps on the left get one more space than the gaps on the right.
  • A line with a single word, and the last line, are left-justified: words are separated by exactly one space and the rest of the line is padded with spaces on the right.

To keep the answer a single token, return all lines joined with the character |, and write every space as an underscore _. Words never contain these characters.

words = "this,is,an,example,of,text,justification", width = 16
-> "this____is____an|example__of_text|justification___"

line 1: this + is + an = 8 letters, 8 spaces over 2 gaps -> 4 + 4
line 2: example + of + text = 13 letters, 3 spaces over 2 gaps -> 2 + 1
line 3 (last): justification, padded on the right

words = "a,b,c", width = 3   -> "a_b|c__"   (a single-word last line is also padded)
constraints: The whole words string has at most 10,000 characters
Words consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Split the work into two phases: first decide which words go on which line, then build each line's text.
Phase 1 is greedy: keep adding the next word while letters so far + (words so far - 1) minimal gaps + next word still fits in width.

Phase 2: for a normal line with g gaps and S spaces to place, every gap gets S // g spaces and the first S % g gaps get one more. Treat the last line and single-word lines separately: single spaces, then pad on the right.
editorial: The two phases are independent. For line breaking, start at word i and extend j while the line made of words i..j separated by single spaces still has at most width characters. Each word is placed once, so this phase is linear in the number of words.

For the layout of a line holding words i..j: if it is the last line or has only one word, join with single spaces and pad on the right. Otherwise let gaps = j - i and spaces = width - letters; give each gap spaces // gaps spaces plus one extra for the first spaces % gaps gaps. Finally replace spaces with underscores and join the lines with | for the single-token output. Every output character is produced once, so the total cost is O(total output length) = O(lines · width).
solution:
def justifyText(words, width):
    ws = words.split(",")
    n = len(ws)
    lines = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i
        total = len(ws[i])
        while j + 1 < n and total + 1 + len(ws[j + 1]) <= width:
            j += 1
            total += 1 + len(ws[j])
        line = ws[i:j + 1]
        if j == n - 1 or len(line) == 1:
            text = " ".join(line)
            text += " " * (width - len(text))
        else:
            gaps = len(line) - 1
            spaces = width - sum(len(w) for w in line)
            q, extra = divmod(spaces, gaps)
            parts = []
            for k in range(gaps):
                parts.append(line[k])
                parts.append(" " * (q + (1 if k < extra else 0)))
            parts.append(line[-1])
            text = "".join(parts)
        lines.append(text.replace(" ", "_"))
        i = j + 1
    return "|".join(lines)
